question: to the Commission Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE) Subject:

Works are under way to expand the marinas in Retelino, Navene and Madonnina, in the municipality of Malcesine (Verona)1. Madonnina boasts an historical lakefront that still has natural and seminatural beaches – increasingly rare sights as the shores of Lake Garda are subject to extensive overdevelopment. The works include dredging, coastline management and extension of the artificial quays. Studies have been performed on sediments and swell but – as the province of Verona and Veneto Region confirmed to the Gruppo d'Intervento Giuridico (Legal Intervention Group) following an inquiry – no procedure has been initiated to screen for an environmental impact assessment (EIA)2, nor has an analysis been conducted of the lake’s ecosystem or animal and plant life, despite the dramatic decline in native fish stocks and the destruction of the lakebed. In time, the lakefront will also be affected by lot 4 of the cycle- and footpath, which will see it double in length and fully disappear under layers of concrete. In the light of the above: 1.

With a view to countering the increasing development of the Garda shoreline, which, together with overtourism, is damaging the lake ecosystem, does the Commission believe that the EIA procedure followed has been applied correctly?
Will it look into what steps need to be taken to restore the natural coastal stretches that have been artificially developed?

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.7.2026) Under Article 4(2) of the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Directive1, for projects listed in Annex II, Member States shall determine whether the project shall be made subject to an assessment. This determination must be made through a case-by-case examination or thresholds or criteria set by the Member States which may decide to apply both procedures. ‘Marinas’ and ‘any change or extension of projects listed in Annex I [or II], already authorised, executed or in the process of being executed, which may have significant adverse effects on the environment…’ fall respectively within the scope of Annex II, point 12(b) and point 13(a) of the EIA Directive. The Commission notes that local organisations have exercised their rights to access environmental information, protected under the Directive on public access to environmental information2 and the Aarhus Convention3, to obtain information on the ongoing environmental decision-making progress. In this regard, the Commission recalls that concerned citizens and environmental organisations also enjoy the right to access to justice, protected under the EIA Directive4 and the Aarhus Convention. It is for the Italian competent authorities to apply the above rules and procedures to this project and to ensure that, if damage to the environment has occurred, it is restored as appropriate. In its role as guardian of the Treaties, the Commission may decide to intervene if systemic problems arise in the application of the provisions of EU law5.
1 Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment

of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (codification), OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, p. 1– 21; Directive 2014/52/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 April 2014 amending Directive 2011/92/EU on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment, OJ L 124, 25.4.2014, p. 1–18. 2 Directive 2003/4/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 January 2003 on public access to environmental information and repealing Council Directive 90/313/EEC OJ L 41, 14.2.2003, pp. 26–32. 3 United Nations Economic Commission for Europe Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation in Decision-making and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters. 4 Article 11 of the EIA Directive. 5 Communication of 19 January 2017 (EU law: Better results through better application - C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20) and in the Communication of 13 October 2022 COM(2022) 518 final - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers.
